header.commentBefore: Supervises the shredder hopper high-level sensor: raises a latched hopper-blockage alarm (and a stop/inhibit demand) when the hopper stays (debounced-)high for a cumulative threshold of time while the plant is running, i.e. the shredder/pusher is not clearing it (S6 request #1, REQ-HBA-001..007). Purely supervisory - it commands no motion and writes no shared tag; the alarm and the stop demand are exposed on its own IO interface and wired to annunciation / the actual stop at a separate integration step (Q-HBA-05). Cumulative timing is pause-and-resume (NEW-HBA-01): losing PlantRunning freezes the elapsed and resumes, so 60 s of blockage need not be contiguous. Built from a plain TON, never TONR (C-406), plus a banked up-accumulator compared against the threshold (see NETWORK 3-4). The alarm latch lives in the RETAIN interface and deliberately survives a power cycle (C-124 carve-out, NEW-HBA-04) - like the sequencer's DischargeConveyorTimeoutFault, a blockage needing a human still needs FaultReset after a restart; all transient timing state is non-retentive and self-clears at startup (NEW-HBA-06, no OB100 edit). Tunables BlockedTimeThreshold (T#60S) and ClearDebounceTime (T#2S) are this instance's own settings (C-307), not shared DB members.

  COMMENT "Integration of the hopper-blockage supervisor (S6 request #1). header.commentBefore: Latches the four states the requirement register forbids outright, so that a forbidden state lasting a single scan is still there to be read a hundred milliseconds later. A forbidden state cannot be sampled: a sampler that looks a hundred times still looks between scans, and a miss reports as a pass rather than as an error - so a latch is the only admissible instrument for a claim of the form 'this never happens', not a convenience. Everything here is computed from what the monitored block already publishes on its own interface and from the stimulus model's own phase; nothing reaches inside the monitored block and nothing writes to it. The latches are armed by the stimulus model's observation window rather than running free from the start of the run, because every run legitimately begins by driving the monitor through a clear-down, and a free-running latch would fill from that and read violated whatever the monitor did. They are cleared when the harness drops the start bool, which is the same point the start echo is cleared.

networks.beforeText:
NETWORK 4 "The Two Outputs Disagreeing"
  COMMENT "The stop demand and the alarm are required to agree, and the two directions are latched separately because one latch on their inequality could not say which way round it went. Note what this pair does not constrain: it is satisfied by both outputs moving together at the wrong moment, so it is evidence about the relation and about nothing else - what pins the pair to the plant is the timing assertions, not these."
  SCOIL InhibitLowWhileAlarmHigh := iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor.IO.HopperBlockedAlarm AND NOT iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor.IO.HopperBlockStopReq AND iDB_HopperBlockageStim.Stim.Armed
  SCOIL InhibitHighWhileAlarmLow := iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor.IO.HopperBlockStopReq AND NOT iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor.IO.HopperBlockedAlarm AND iDB_HopperBlockageStim.Stim.Armed
